title: Introduce unit-econ-audit CLI and conservative quant profiles
author: Amina Patel
description: Motivation: teams need a low-friction, auditable way to validate unit economics before rolling quantization or batching defaults into production. This PR adds a lightweight CLI tool (unit-econ-audit) that simulates request mixes, applies conservative quantization profiles, and produces an audit report with token-level cost projections and tail-latency risk bands. Summary: add CLI wrapper, new conservative quant profile YAMLs, a small simulation engine that reuses existing sampling primitives, integration tests, and docs. The CLI is intentionally conservative by default (won't recommend aggressive int8 fallbacks) and outputs a set of recommended safe profiles plus warnings for tail latency or accuracy risk. Checklist: - [x] Implement CLI entrypoint and flags for workload slice, sample size, and risk tolerance. - [x] Add conservative quant profile catalog and profile validator. - [x] Reuse workload sampler framework and extend sample tiler for bursty arrival patterns. - [x] Add unit + integration tests and fixtures. - [x] Add docs and a usage example (dev docs and example repo snippet). - [x] Add Linear ticket references and changelog entry. Commits summary: 1) feat(auditor): initial simulator and CLI scaffolding, 2) feat(profiles): add conservative quant catalog and validator, 3) perf(sampling): extend sample tiler to model microbursts and tail latency, 4) test: add integration scenario for tenant-like traffic, 5) docs: usage guide and example walkthrough. Changed areas (high-level): - rwb/tools/unit_econ_audit.py: new CLI and orchestration glue. - rwb/sampling/tiler.py: extend tiler with bursty pattern generator and deterministic seeding. - rwb/quant/profiles/conservative/*.yml: three new conservative profiles for GPU/CPU/edge tiers. - rwb/quant/validator.py: profile schema validator and safety checks. - rwb/tests/integration/test_unit_econ_audit.py: adds end-to-end scenario. - docs/dev/unit-econ-audit.md: walkthrough and examples. - examples/cost-audit/sample-config.json: sample config for customers. Review notes and conversation: - Evan: "Nice end-to-end story; can we expose an option to export recommendations as a JSON policy for the defaults compiler?" Reply (Amina): "Yes, added --export-policy flag to CLI and documented mapping to defaults compiler schema." - Priya: "How are we measuring accuracy regressions for quant profiles?" Reply: "CLI runs a small eval set when --eval-path is provided and reports relative delta; we also emit warnings when delta crosses the risk tolerance threshold." - Marcel: "Integration CI flaked on the tiler seed; make seeding deterministic for test mode." Reply: "Fixed: added --seed and deterministic mode used by tests." CI and stability: initial CI run failed one integration test because of non-deterministic tiler seeding; test retried with deterministic seed and all checks passed. Lint, unit tests and integration scenario run in under 12 minutes on CI. Security review: no secrets, CLI only reads local files; profile validator prevents malformed YAML from being applied. Performance: lightweight simulator targets <1s/sample for default sample sizes; larger sims are limited by --sample-size. Backwards compatibility: conservative profiles and CLI are additive; no behavior change to runtime defaults until exported policies are applied. Merge outcome: merged via squash with commit message summarizing feature and linking ENG-5123. Release notes: "Add unit-econ-audit CLI: simulate workload mixes with conservative quant profiles and export safe policy recommendations for defaults compiler. Useful for pre-flight cost/regression checks." Notes for backport: none. Manual steps: update docs site navigation to include the new dev guide (will be done in docs release PR).
